mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby lowering S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day period.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in the next 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day high-rate period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS increases by at least 10,000 in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.05) when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a simultaneous rise in retail sales (not available in the catalog) would indicate shifting demand patterns, but since only INDPRO is available, a sharp drop in INDPRO followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a short-term S&P 500 rally over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant improvement over the prior 60-day downleg (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, which typically precede inflationary pressures that can drive S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO shows three consecutive monthly declines
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not lower than the average during the prior 60 days of expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a policy shift, causing a sharp discount in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% and remains above for at least 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30 days of sub-2% inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not available) or a rapid increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates optimism about labor market resilience, driving S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% while PAYEMS increases by at least 20,000 in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns fail to exceed the prior 5-day average when both triggers are met (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in consumer spending proxies (none available) or a combination of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL) and rising real wages (not available) would typically signal a soft landing, but using available data, a steady decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% for 4 months predicts a S&P 500 positive 60-day forward return as market anticipates rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of declining consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and a simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), the market expects future rate stability, which can compress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.5% while CPIAUCSL declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day high-rate, low-inflation window (t-test p > 0.05).
